instruction: Convert all .doc files in the current directory to ODT format using the command line.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully listed .doc files on Desktop, then ran 'libreoffice --headless --convert-to pdf *.doc' to convert all 12 .doc files to PDF. Conversion completed with all PDFs generated correctly.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can use terminal, run libreoffice headless commands, list files, wait for long-running conversions
metadata.task_rationale: Same pattern as original (batch libreoffice conversion) but targeting a different output format (ODT instead of PDF), testing the model's knowledge of supported libreoffice output formats.
metadata.explanation: Task requires converting .doc files to .odt format using libreoffice --headless --convert-to odt *.doc. Evaluator checks bash history for the correct command pattern and verifies 12 .odt files exist on Desktop.

scoring_breakdown.command_found: 0.4 - Correct libreoffice --convert-to odt command found in bash history

llm_judge_reasons: Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule': directly accesses expected.get('expected_odt_count', 12) which is correct since framework passes rules dict directly
Getter correctly counts .odt files on Desktop using ls/wc-l, providing robust primary verification (0.6 weight) of the conversion outcome
Getter checks bash history for libreoffice/soffice --convert-to odt pattern, verifying the 'using command line' requirement (0.4 weight)
Coverage is complete: both 'convert to ODT' (file count check) and 'using command line' (history check) requirements are verified

Minor concern: postconfig kills gnome-terminal-server which may prevent bash from flushing history to ~/.bash_history, potentially causing the history check (0.4 weight) to fail even when the correct command was used
Minor concern: history grep pattern requires '*.doc' glob specifically - agents using individual filenames or different glob patterns would not get the 0.4 command credit
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding a postconfig step to explicitly flush bash history before killing the terminal (e.g., 'bash -c "kill -SIGHUP $(pgrep -f gnome-terminal)"' or reading from /proc/*/cmdline instead of bash_history)
Consider broadening the history grep pattern to also match individual file conversions (e.g., 'libreoffice.*--convert-to\s+odt') without requiring '*.doc' at the end
